{{Short description|Unsolved conjecture in geometry}}
In [[arithmetic geometry]], the '''Bombieri–Lang conjecture''' is an unsolved problem [[conjecture]]d by [[Enrico Bombieri]] and [[Serge Lang]] about the [[Zariski topology|Zariski density]] of the set of [[rational point]]s of an [[algebraic variety]] of [[Kodaira dimension#General type|general type]].

==Statement==
The weak Bombieri–Lang conjecture for surfaces states that if <math>X</math> is a smooth [[surface of general type]] defined over a [[number field]] <math>k</math>, then the {{nowrap|<math>k</math>-rational}} points of <math>X</math> do not form a [[dense set]] in the [[Zariski topology]] on <math>X</math>.<ref name="Das-Turchet"/>

The general form of the Bombieri–Lang conjecture states that if <math>X</math> is a positive-dimensional algebraic variety of general type defined over a number field <math>k</math>, then the {{nowrap|<math>k</math>-rational}} points of <math>X</math> do not form a dense set in the Zariski topology.<ref name="Poonen"/><ref name="CUV"/><ref name="Hindry-Silverman"/>

The refined form of the Bombieri–Lang conjecture states that if <math>X</math> is an algebraic variety of general type defined over a number field <math>k</math>, then there is a dense [[open subset]] <math>U</math> of <math>X</math> such that for all number field extensions <math>k'</math> over <math>k</math>, the set of {{nowrap|<math>k'</math>-rational}} points in <math>U</math> is finite.<ref name="Hindry-Silverman"/>

==History==
The Bombieri–Lang conjecture was independently posed by Enrico Bombieri and Serge Lang. In a 1980 lecture at the [[University of Chicago]], Enrico Bombieri posed a problem about the degeneracy of rational points for surfaces of general type.<ref name="Das-Turchet">{{citation ==Generalizations and implications==
The Bombieri–Lang conjecture is an analogue for surfaces of [[Faltings' theorem]], which states that algebraic curves of [[genus (mathematics)|genus]] greater than one only have finitely many rational points.<ref name="Tao">{{citation
 | last = Tao | first = Terence | author-link = Terence Tao
 | date = December 20, 2014
 | title = The Erdos-Ulam problem, varieties of general type, and the Bombieri-Lang conjecture
 | url = https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2014/12/20/the-erdos-ulam-problem-varieties-of-general-type-and-the-bombieri-lang-conjecture/
 | work = What's new}}</ref>

If true, the Bombieri–Lang conjecture would resolve the [[Erdős–Ulam problem]], as it would imply that there do not exist dense subsets of the Euclidean plane all of whose pairwise distances are rational.<ref name="Tao"/><ref>{{citation |last1=Shaffaf |first1=Jafar |title=A solution of the Erdős–Ulam problem on rational distance sets assuming the Bombieri–Lang conjecture |journal=[[Discrete & Computational Geometry]] |date=May 2018 |volume=60 |issue=8 |pages=283–293 |doi=10.1007/s00454-018-0003-3|arxiv=1501.00159 }}</ref>

In 1997, [[Lucia Caporaso]], [[Barry Mazur]], [[Joe Harris (mathematician)|Joe Harris]], and Patricia Pacelli showed that the Bombieri–Lang conjecture implies a [[uniform boundedness conjecture for rational points]]: there is a constant <math>B_{g,d}</math> depending only on <math>g</math> and <math>d</math> such that the number of rational points of any genus <math>g</math> curve <math>X</math> over any [[Degree of a field extension|degree]] <math>d</math> number field is at most <math>B_{g,d}</math>.<ref name="Poonen">{{citation |first=Bjorn |last=Poonen |author-link=Bjorn Poonen |title= Uniform boundedness of rational points and preperiodic points |arxiv= 1206.7104 |year=2012}}</ref><ref name="CUV">{{citation |title=Unboundedness of the number of rational points on curves over function fields |last1=Conceição |first1=Ricardo |last2=Ulmer |first2=Douglas |authorlink2=Douglas Ulmer |last3=Voloch |first3=José Felipe |authorlink3= José Felipe Voloch |journal=New York Journal of Mathematics |volume=18 |year=2012 |pages=291–293}}</ref>
